ActivationBudget.description: Hard limits of one Activation (accumulated over its runs).

oneOf.description: Looked, nothing to do now (not "achieved").
No valid result was submitted.

missed.description: Slots that passed while no fire was possible (`scheduled`).

oneOf.description: A Work of the Goal finished (or needs attention).
A message handed over from a UI.
Any other subscribed event (a followed task, an object).
A question of the Goal was answered (or closed) by the user: `ref` is its notification.

Activity.description: What this session is doing and roughly what it modifies (§6.7).

CallTrigger.description: How a sub context was called, i.e. where its result returns to.

oneOf.description: `next_behavior` of a complete Step: the result returns as `process_result` in the caller's hand-over batch.
A tool call / behavior action: the caller is suspended on `PendingTool`, the result is filled as the tool result of `call_id`.

ChildCall.description: The sub context a `Caller` frame waits for.

task.description: Task given to the child (tool trigger: the call's `task` argument).

ContextMode.description: How a behavior is entered when a hand-over (`next_behavior`) or a `call_behavior` tool call names it. Decided by the target behavior, never by the session as a whole; there is no default mode.

oneOf.description: The target has its own context (system, tools, history, run): created on first entry, resumed from its own snapshot afterwards.
A new sub context per call with the target's system and task input, plus an explicit selection of the caller's history; its result returns to the caller.
A new branch per call that keeps the caller's system and its complete effective history at the fork point; its result returns to the caller.
A restart opened the next epoch (the Work keeps running).

id.description: object: object id; session: sid; task: task_id; timer: timer name; system: may be empty.

kind.description: `object | session | task | timer | system`; unknown kinds are not a format error (an event without a matching subscription is dropped).

oneOf.description: A context left through SWITCH_CONTEXT: re-entered when a hand-over names its entry again.
The caller of a sub context (create-sub-context / fork): live again when the child returns.

result.description: The submitted Goal result, as accepted.

seq.description: = the Turn index of the epoch's Goal Session.

GoalEnding.description: How the Goal Session ends (decided by its Goal).

cascade.description: The Goal's running Work is stopped too (archive).

notify_id.description: The notification that asks it (none: not sent, or no notification service).

GoalSessionState.description: `state.json.goal` of a Goal Session: the Goal State the session owns (committed with the session, published to `state/goals/<id>/state.json` afterwards), Activation records not appended yet, the open Activation.

GoalSkill.description: A method / capability the Goal works with (architecture §10.2).

ref.description: Where it is read (path, object id, behavior name).

absorbed.description: Work whose end was taken in by an Activation (any epoch; bounded).

goal_revision_seen.description: Goal revision the last Activation worked with.

questions.description: Questions for the user: sent as notifications when the host has a notification service; answers come back as `answer` Activations.

GoalUsage.description: Usage of the current statistics period.

tokens.description: Tokens of the Goal Session's Activations.

work_tokens.description: Tokens of the Work absorbed in the period.

GoalWork.description: A Work of the Goal not absorbed yet.

InputPos.description: Delivery position of a bus record.

LiveRun.description: A run that is not finished yet (xllm run directory).

applied_input_seq.description: Receipt batches of this run already applied to state (§8.3).

flushed_epoch.description: History epoch (`HostMeta.history_epoch`) `flushed_message_count` counts in. A snapshot of a newer epoch starts at zero: its whole history before the rewrite was flushed before the rewrite was published.

flushed_input_seq.description: Behavior runs: receipts (injected messages) with `input_seq ≤` this are in the worklog.

flushed_message_count.description: Function call runs: messages after the history prefix (within `flushed_epoch`) already in the worklog.

flushed_step_index.description: Behavior runs: steps with `step_index <` this are in the worklog (identity high-water mark, not a count: inherited steps of a fork child and steps rewritten away are never written).

handover_at_ms.description: `at_ms` of the run's hand-over record (run.json `handover`) this state already committed: a record with this stamp is not a transfer left to do.

process_entry.description: Process entry the run belongs to (behavior process ↔ run).

OpenActivation.description: The Activation in progress of a Goal Session (= its open Turn).

budget.description: Effective limits, frozen when it opened. Its tokens and runs are those of the `usage.jsonl` records after `usage_offset`.

usage_offset.description: Length of the session's `usage.jsonl` when it opened: its tokens are the records after it.

OpenTurn.description:
The logical Turn in progress (one Input → result of the AgentSession).

Opened by the first input batch committed while no Turn is open (bootstrap, msg / event). Context switches, sub context calls and returns, observation injections, resumable suspensions (interrupt, retryable error, context limit, pending tool), history epoch rewrites and restarts keep it open; inputs consumed while it is open join it. Only the session closes it, when it interprets an outcome as the Turn's result or failure ([`TurnStatus`]).

has_msg.description: A message (not only events) is among them.

inputs.description: msg / event inputs that make up the Turn's logical input: those of the opening batch, then those consumed while it was open.

run_id.description: Input batch that opened it: `(run_id, input_seq)`.

OutboxEntry.description: One outbound message of a session.

msg.description: The complete message, `created_at_ms` included: re-sent unchanged.

OutboxPurpose.description: What an outbox entry is for.

oneOf.description: The reply of a Turn as a message of its own.
"Accepted, working on it": sent while the Turn is open, replaced by the Turn's final edit.
The reply of a Turn as an edit of its placeholder.
A question to the user while the Turn is open (`ask-user`): a `thread` message on the placeholder, carrying `agent_ask`.
Not handed to the outbound sink yet, or the hand-over failed in a way worth retrying.
Refused (route mismatch, rejected by the message service); never retried.

PendingEvent.description: Semi-subscription state waiting to be injected: the newest version of one `(subscription_id, source)`, its terminal event kept separately. Saved when received (the delivery is then consumed); cleared only by the receipt of the batch that injected exactly these versions, by `unsubscribe`, or replaced by a newer version.

superseded.description: Versions replaced before they were injected.

terminal.description: Never replaced by later non-terminal versions.

PendingEventVersion.description: One version of an observed source's state.

input.description: Where it was delivered (`None`: synthesized by the runner, e.g. a pull-mode session subscription).

ProcessFrame.description: Suspended behavior process (its run is kept, §4.4).

call.description: `Caller` frames: the child being waited for.

handover_at_ms.description: `at_ms` of the hand-over record this suspension committed (see [`LiveRun::handover_at_ms`]).

RecentKeys.description: Bounded dedup cache of producer `key`s (§4.5). It only filters duplicate deliveries; it never replaces the receipts persisted in snapshots or the per-source consumption positions.

ReplyRoute.description: Default reply path of a session.

oneOf.description: Reply the way the last consumed input message came.

reply_to.description: ObjId of the message replied to.

oneOf.description: Hand the result back to the parent session.

ReportArtifact.description: One artifact of a report: a file of the work directory (`path`, copied to `reference`) or a named object (`path` is its id). `obj_id` is what leaves the session: the submitted id, or the file put into the host's object store (`None`: the host has none, or storing failed).

SourceProgress.description: Consumption progress of one input source (§4.5).

accepted.description: Input events accepted by an active subscription that are still pending: their routing was decided when they were first seen, so a later `unsubscribe` does not turn them into dropped events.

acked_index.description: Highest index acknowledged-able: every index ≤ this was consumed.

TurnInputs.description: Inputs of one logical Turn that entered a run. The input batch that opens the Turn (or the first batch of an already open Turn in this run) starts an entry; later batches of the same Turn (hand-over, observation, supplementary input) extend it, so the list grows with Turns, not with batches.

events.description: Keys of the semi-subscription state versions injected with them.

hook.description: Controlled input of the first batch (`on_init`, `on_input`, `on_context_switch`).

input_seq.description: `input_seq` of the first batch of this Turn in the run.

TurnStatus.description: How a logical Turn ended (decided by the session from the outcome and the hand-over state, never by the waist alone).

oneOf.description: A result was delivered (final answer, a reply before waiting for input, or the session finished).
A non-recoverable error ended the run.
The run's budget was exhausted.
`control(stop)`.

TurnTask.description: A Turn and the task the host's task service keeps for it. Written when the task was created (the Turn is open), closed in the commit that closes the Turn, `reported` once the task service took the terminal state.

has_msg.description: The batch that opened the Turn had a message: a placeholder may be sent for it.

placeholder.description: ObjId of the placeholder message of this Turn (the anchor its final edit targets).

summary.description: Result summary handed to the task service with the terminal state.

human_tasks.description: TaskMgr human tasks the wait depends on: questions asked through a notification (`ask-user` of a Work).

WaitingKind.description: What a waiting session waits for (`waiting_for.kind`).

goal.description: Goal Sessions: the Goal State it owns and the Activation in progress.

inputs.description: Per input source consumption progress, keyed by source id.

internal_continuation.description: An input batch to commit without new input (context switch, sub context call / return through `next_behavior`); it joins the open Turn.

open_turn.description: The Turn in progress, if any.

outbox.description: Replies produced by committed Turns and their delivery: written in the commit that closes the Turn, sent afterwards, re-sent as they are after a restart (the idempotency key and the message never change).

pending_decision.description: Decisions seen in the queue but not applied yet (UI display).

pending_events.description: Semi-subscription state received and not injected yet.

process_result.description: Result of a sub context, handed to its caller: `{behavior, result, status: ok | failed | needs_user_input, next_action_id, next_step_index}`. Behavior trigger: rendered into the caller's hand-over batch. Tool trigger: carries `call_id` and is filled as that call's tool result when the caller's run is opened.

reply.description: Default reply path: the way the last consumed input message came, else the parent session.

stop_requested.description: Stop requested through `control(stop)`; applied at the next safe point.

subscription_cursors.description: Pull-mode cursors only (registry rev of session subscriptions).

turn_seq.description: Number of the latest Turn opened (0 before the first input batch).

turn_stop_requested.description: Only the open Turn is to be stopped (`control(stop, scope = turn)`, or any stop of a Goal Session): the session goes on waiting afterwards.

turn_tasks.description: Turns bound to a task of the host's task service: the open Turn's, closed ones whose terminal state is not reported yet, and the most recent settled ones.

watched_tasks.description: Background tasks of ended runs the runner follows for this session (implicit active subscriptions on `task:<task_id>`): when one ends, its completion is handled like a subscribed event.
